findings.name: stock-db
findings.root_cause: stock-db container has a 24Mi memory limit but its workload loads a stock index into memory and keeps growing, so the kernel OOM-kills it (exit 137) every ~50s; the dead DB makes stock-db:5432 unreachable, so stock-api fails its 3 connection attempts and exits.
findings.fix: Raise the stock-db Deployment's memory request/limit well above 24Mi (e.g. 256Mi or more, based on observed peak of the stock-index load) so the container stops being OOMKilled; this restores stock-db:5432 and stops stock-api crash loops.

diagnosis.summary: stock-api crash-loops because its database stock-db is unavailable: stock-db's container is OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts, BackOff events) because its 24Mi memory limit is far below what its in-memory stock-index load needs. The API logs show repeated 'stock-db:5432 unreachable' then FATAL exit after 3 attempts. Root cause object: Deployment stock-db — raise its memory limit. stock-api is a victim and should recover once the DB stays up.

findings.name: billing
findings.root_cause: The billing container uses envFrom on ConfigMap "billing-config", which does not exist in the namespace, so kubelet cannot create the container (CreateContainerConfigError) and the pod stays Pending.
findings.fix: Create the missing ConfigMap billing-config in namespace billing with the expected keys (or remove the envFrom reference if it is no longer needed), then let the Deployment recreate its pod.

diagnosis.summary: billing never reaches Running because its pod is stuck in CreateContainerConfigError: the container's envFrom references ConfigMap \"billing-config\", which does not exist in the billing namespace (only kube-root-ca.crt is present). Creating that ConfigMap (or removing the envFrom reference) will unblock the rollout.

findings.name: orders-api
findings.root_cause: orders-api container exits 1 on startup with 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set' because the Deployment defines no env or envFrom at all, so it crash-loops (5 restarts, BackOff) and has 0 ready replicas, taking the orders page down.
findings.fix: Add DATABASE_URL to the orders-api Deployment (env or an envFrom referencing a Secret/ConfigMap that holds it), then roll out.

diagnosis.summary: orders/orders-api crash-loops: its only container logs 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set' and exits 1 (5 restarts, BackOff event). The Deployment spec has no env/envFrom and the namespace has no ConfigMap providing config, so the required DATABASE_URL is simply missing from the pod spec. No other problem pods in the namespace; the down orders page is explained by 0 ready replicas of orders-api."

findings.name: mailer
findings.root_cause: Mailer pod uses dnsPolicy None with nameserver 10.96.0.99 which cannot resolve 'smtp-relay'. The relay pod and service are healthy, but nc fails with 'bad address', causing exit code 1 and crashloop.
findings.fix: Remove the custom dnsPolicy/dnsConfig from the mailer Deployment so it inherits ClusterFirst DNS, which will resolve smtp-relay correctly.

diagnosis.summary: The smtp-relay is NOT down — its pod is running, ready, and listening on port 25 with a valid service endpoint. The real problem is the mailer Deployment: it sets dnsPolicy: None with a hardcoded nameserver 10.96.0.99 that cannot resolve in-cluster service names. As a result, `nc smtp-relay 25` fails with 'bad address', the mailer exits with code 1, and the pod crash-loops. Fix: remove the custom dnsPolicy/dnsConfig from the mailer Deployment spec so it uses the default ClusterFirst DNS.

diagnosis.summary: media/thumbnailer pods are repeatedly evicted: the log-shipper sidecar buffers 4Mi batches to an emptyDir while the upstream collector is unreachable, exceeding its 20Mi ephemeral-storage limit in a few minutes. Kubelet evicts the pod and the Deployment recreates it, matching the reported 'disappearing every few minutes' behavior. Root cause is the thumbnailer Deployment spec (sidecar storage limit vs unbounded buffering); fix the collector connectivity and right-size/cap the buffer.

findings.name: accounts-api
findings.root_cause: Init container wait-for-db loops forever because it probes host 'accounts-db:5432', but the database Service is named 'accounts-database' (the only service in the namespace); 'accounts-db' does not exist, so nc fails with 'bad address' and the main container never starts.
findings.fix: Point the init container at the real service name: change 'nc -z -w 2 accounts-db 5432' to 'nc -z -w 2 accounts-database 5432' in the accounts-api Deployment's initContainer command (or rename the Service to accounts-db).

diagnosis.summary: accounts-api pod is stuck in Init:Running for ~20 minutes. The init container wait-for-db repeatedly fails with "nc: bad address 'accounts-db'" because no Service named accounts-db exists; the database Service is actually named accounts-database (healthy, 1 ready endpoint on 5432). Fix: update the init container command in the accounts-api Deployment to probe accounts-database:5432.

findings.name: nightly-export
findings.root_cause: Both job pods exited 2 with 'permission denied: cannot write /exports/orders-2026-09-27.csv' — the pod mounts no writable volume at /exports, so no file was produced and the job hit its backoff limit.
findings.fix: Give the job a writable destination for /exports (mount an emptyDir or PVC there, or fix container write permissions) and re-run the Job after deleting it.

diagnosis.summary: The exports/nightly-export Job produced no file because both pods (lhlrb, mjzfj) terminated with exit code 2 on 'permission denied: cannot write /exports/orders-2026-09-27.csv'. The pod spec mounts nothing at /exports (no volumes, no PVC in the namespace), so the app cannot create its output; the job then exceeded its backoff limit (BackoffLimitExceeded). Fix is to provide a writable volume at /exports in the Job spec."

diagnosis.summary: statement-builder in finance OOM-kills despite having no explicit memory limit because the namespace LimitRange 'defaults' applies a 32Mi default memory limit to containers that don't set one. The job loads ~50MB of ledger rows into memory, exceeding 32Mi, so the container is killed with exit 137 and back-off restarts. Fix by setting an explicit, adequate memory limit on the Deployment (or adjusting the LimitRange).

findings.name: checkout
findings.root_cause: Service checkout selects app=checkout-v2, but the checkout Deployment's pods are labeled app=checkout, so the selector matches 0 pods and the service has no endpoints; clients connecting through the ClusterIP get connection refused even though the pod itself is healthy and serving on port 80.
findings.fix: Align the Service selector with the pod labels: set spec.selector to app=checkout (or relabel the Deployment pods to app=checkout-v2), then verify ready endpoints appear.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout pods are healthy (1/1 Ready, nginx on :80), but the checkout Service selects app=checkout-v2 while the Deployment's pods are labeled app=checkout. Result: 0 matching pods, 0 ready endpoints, and connection refused for callers of the service. Root cause is the Service selector mismatch; fix by aligning the selector to app=checkout.

findings.name: report-worker
findings.root_cause: The report-worker container is OOMKilled (exit 137) within seconds of starting because its memory limit is only 32Mi (request 16Mi); the process exceeds the limit before it can do useful work, so it restarts in a loop with no application error in its logs.
findings.fix: Raise the report-worker container memory limit (e.g. from 32Mi to at least 128Mi, matching observed usage) and bump the request accordingly; verify actual working-set size first if the workload genuinely needs more.

diagnosis.summary: report-worker pod in namespace reports is crash-looping: every container instance is OOMKilled (exit 137) shortly after start, causing BackOff restarts. The Deployment sets a 32Mi memory limit / 16Mi request, which the process exceeds immediately, so it dies without writing any app-level error log. Root cause is the undersized memory limit on the report-worker Deployment; fix by raising the memory limit/request.

findings.name: cache
findings.root_cause: Pod cache-54f4fcc74-25gpc stays Pending because its nodeSelector requires disktype=nvme, but the only node (doctor-lab-control-plane) is labeled disktype=standard, so 0/1 nodes match and no pod can ever run.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the nodeSelector on the cache Deployment (change disktype from nvme to standard, or drop it if no NVMe requirement exists).

diagnosis.summary: The cache deployment never gets a pod running because its pod template carries nodeSelector disktype=nvme, while the cluster's only node doctor-lab-control-plane is labeled disktype=standard. The scheduler reports '0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', leaving the pod permanently Pending and the Deployment at 0 ready replicas. Fix: remove or correct the nodeSelector on the cache Deployment.

findings.name: ml-trainer
findings.root_cause: ml-trainer requests 64 CPU cores while the cluster's only node (doctor-lab-control-plane) has 2 allocatable CPU, so the scheduler reports 'Insufficient cpu' and the pod stays Pending; preemption is not helpful because no existing workload could free 62+ cores.
findings.fix: Lower the ml-trainer container CPU request to fit within the node's 2 allocatable cores (e.g. 1 or 2), or add nodes with enough CPU capacity.

diagnosis.summary: ml-trainer has been Pending because its Deployment sets a CPU request of 64 cores on a cluster whose single node offers only 2 allocatable CPU. Scheduler events confirm 'Insufficient cpu' and that preemption cannot help. Fix: reduce the CPU request to at most ~2 cores (or scale out the cluster). No other workloads are affected.

findings.name: pricing-api
findings.root_cause: Calls to pricing-api fail with connection refused because the Service forwards to targetPort 8080 while the nginx container only listens on port 80; nothing listens on 8080 in the pod, so every proxied connection is refused even though the pod passes its readiness probe (port 80) and reports Ready.
findings.fix: Change the pricing-api Service targetPort from 8080 to 80 to match the container's actual listen port (or set the container to listen on 8080).

diagnosis.summary: pricing-api pods are healthy and ready (readiness probe hits port 80, which nginx serves), but the Service pricing-api forwards traffic to targetPort 8080 where nothing listens, so all calls fail with connection refused. Root cause is the Service port mismatch; fix by pointing targetPort at 80.

findings.name: search-web
findings.root_cause: The liveness probe runs a 300,000-iteration busy loop before the wget health check and has only a 1s timeout, so it always times out; kubelet kills the (healthy) container, which restarts with exit code 0 — hence no errors in the app logs.
findings.fix: Fix the search-web Deployment's livenessProbe: remove the busy-loop from the exec command (just 'wget -q -O /dev/null http://127.0.0.1/') and/or raise timeoutSeconds above 1s.

diagnosis.summary: search-web crash-loops not because the app fails but because its liveness probe is broken: the exec probe runs a 300k-iteration shell loop before the wget check with a 1s timeout, so it always times out (event ev-eefcb9). Kubelet then kills the healthy container (exit code 0, 'Completed'), producing CrashLoopBackOff with clean logs. Fix the probe in the search-web Deployment spec.

findings.fix: Re-issue the auth-api server cert from Internal Services CA 2026 (SANs auth-api.identity.svc, auth-api.identity.svc.cluster.local, auth-api), update ConfigMap auth-api-cert and the auth-api-tls secret, restart auth-api pods.
findings.name: auth-api-cert
findings.root_cause: session-svc returns 502 on /login: its nginx verifies upstream auth-api with the internal CA, but the auth-api server cert in ConfigMap auth-api-cert expired 2026-09-26, so TLS handshakes fail with 'certificate has expired'.

diagnosis.summary: Logins 502 through identity/session-svc because the auth-api server certificate expired. session-svc nginx logs show 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)' proxying /login to https://auth-api:443, returning 502. The trusted CA (internal-ca) is valid to 2036, but the published auth-api cert (auth-api-cert/tls.crt, CN=auth-api, same issuer) expired 2026-09-26 (days_left -1). Fix: re-issue the auth-api cert from the internal CA and update auth-api-cert/auth-api-tls.
